To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
in Punjab villages of the late 1960s lactation prolonged postpartum birth intervals by 9-12 months, and that this was the main factor in the high birth rates in these villages.

in the villages studied in India the average length of birth interval was approximately 3 years and that in these villages the length of birth interval varied inversely with the mother's age at the time of birth.

in a rural area of India where the infant mortality rate is 200 per 1000 live births and where birth control practices are almost non-existent the average birth interval of 32.2 months is prolonged by lactation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the physiology of human lactation and its relation to birth intervals in a variety of human societies.
the physiology of human reproductive processes and the application of such studies to the control of human fertility and to the understanding of the social implications of fertility control.
two major areas of investigation: 1 the physiology of human lactation and 2 the effects of lactation upon birth intervals.

the length of postpartuma amenorrhea is determined primarily by the duration of lactation which in turn is determined largely by the infant's survival.
